_authority_hierarchy: 1. Addenda & Clarifications supersede everything they touch
2. Scope of Work narrative decides WHICH package carries an item
3. Specifications decide HOW the work is executed
4. Drawings show extent and location (weakest authority for assignment)
Proposals are NOT in the hierarchy -- diagnostic only

Provide all trash dumpsters for this scope of work as may be required.

Immediately cease work and coordinate with Contractor for remediation and disposal of any unidentified hazardous materials encountered during course of this work.

scope_items_verbatim: Scope of Work – Temporary Construction Requirements & Dust Control – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Provide minimum 10,000 s.f. construction trailer pad of fractured rock. Grade and install gravel at contractor parking and laydown areas as shown on the Logistics Plan.

Construct and maintain for the duration of the Project, and remove at completion, Department of Air Quality required trackout lengths consisting of both trackout rock and rumble plates at all vehicular entrances. There will be at least two (2) entrances as indicated on Logistics Plan.
Clean and maintain trucking access routes for all equipment, including street sweeping as required for this scope of work only.

Supply and install stand tank for duration of project. Provide temporary water piping from nearest hydrant to stand tank, if needed. Include temporary waterline to trailer area. Jones valve is provided by Contractor.

Subcontractor shall prepare, submit, and obtain Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) for the project site. Scope of work shall include installation and maintenance of all controls, and performing required maintenance documentation for the duration of the Subcontractor’s scope of work.
Provide dust control for all operations related to this scope of work per Nye County Air Quality requirements.

Scope of Work – Building Wrecking – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Demolish and remove from site existing Modular Concessions Building, including foundations.

Remove all below-grade improvements including Foundations and Utility services within a 5’ boundary of the existing building footprints. Cut and cap utilities.
Include all sawcutting as necessary to complete this scope of work.

Scope of Work – Site Clearing / Demolition – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Salvage and turnover to Contractor items scheduled to be salvaged.
Coordinate with Contractor for removal, protection, and storage / turnover as required.
Coordinate with Electrical Subcontractor to ensure dry utilities are capped/made-safe, and equipment salvage has been completed, prior to demolition activities.
Subcontractor shall provide all site demolition and disposal of items disconnected by others, including all abandoned conduit and feeders as indicated.
Perform all Wet Utilities Demolition work including excavation of existing underground wet utilities.
Remove and dispose of existing domestic water lines from existing backflow preventor to 5’ outside existing building.
Remove and dispose of existing sewer water lines from existing manhole to 5’ outside existing building.
Abandon in place existing below grade utilities not uncovered during Earthwork activities, unless specifically scheduled for removal.
Include all photographs and documentation of existing conditions as indicated.
Demolish existing curbs, gutters, asphalt & concrete paving, including existing running track surfacing and subsurfacing.
Demolish existing fencing & gates in its entirety, including foundations / footings.
Demolish existing field lighting & light poles, and flag pole, including foundations / footings.
Demolish existing pressbox and bleachers, including foundations / footings as indicated and required.
Demolish existing athletic equipment, including foundations / footings as indicated and required.
Football goal posts.
Track & field equipment as indicated, including landing pit materials.
Include all sawcutting as required.

Provide tree removal, including stump grinding and removal, as indicated and required.
Coordinate with Landscape Subcontractor for continued irrigation of trees to remain.
Clear site of existing organics, non-organic waste, refuse, and unsatisfactory materials with haul-off and legal off-site disposal.
Includes removal of weeds at landscape planter areas within the limits of work as indicated.
Remove from site and legally dispose of all demolished materials.
Protect in place all items to remain, including electrical transformer, utilities vaults, etc.

Scope of Work – Domestic Water Distribution System – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install domestic water system including tie-in to existing backflow, piping, fittings, valves, and all related components and appurtenances required for a complete system.
Provide ductile iron, copper, and/or PVC water system piping, fittings, valves, and thrust blocks as indicated and required.
Supply and install all reducers, gate valves, and all water and fire water utility lines including all indicated bends and tee’s, at all indicated points of connection.
Perform multiple flush and tests as required by Tonopah Public Utilities.  Disinfect and chlorinate water lines.  Provide written documentation of all flush procedures and testing.
Provide GPS as-builts of all underground domestic water.  Provide drafted plan upon completion of utility scope.

Scope of Work – Sanitary Sewer System – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install sanitary sewer system including tie-in to existing manhole, piping, fittings, and all related components and appurtenances required for a complete system.
Include shoring as required for deep manholes, if required.
Supply and install concrete encasement of new sanitary sewer piping at water crossings where separation distances cannot be maintained, as required.
Subcontractor shall camera all sanitary sewer piping to 5’ outside of building, and provide video documentation to Contractor for acceptance.
Provide GPS as-builts of all underground sanitary sewer utilities.  Provide AutoCAD file and drafted plan upon completion of utility scope.

Supply and install perforated storm drain system along straight sides of turf system as indicated and detailed.
Supply and install prefabricated trench drains as detailed.

scope_items_verbatim: Scope of Work – Site Concrete – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

Supply and place concrete and reinforcement for all concrete flatwork; athletic equipment pads, curbs, take-off boards, and associated concrete items as indicated; and turndown edges, including all layout.
Supply and install concrete curbs at Synthetic Turf Sports Field and Running Track.
Supply and install slot drain / trench drains and concrete curb along track perimeter and as indicated per detail D/L1.03, including all excavation, trenching, bedding, and backfill.

Includes all piping, radius slot drains, storm drain collector pipe, concrete encasements as required, cleanouts, and all storm water drainage structures as indicated and required for a complete slot drain storm drainage system.
Connection to site storm drainage system by others. Storm drainage system not related to slot / trench drainage system by others.
Supply and install concrete pads at equipment pads, including transformer pad.
Provide keyed joints, saw cutting, control joints, and expansion joints as indicated and required.
Provide expansion joints filler and sealants as required. Place and strip white cap at all expansion joints.
Provide control joint layout shop drawings for architectural approval.
Dowel all exterior sidewalks to the building slab at entrances and doorways, whether or not detailed on drawings.
Provide and install 5/8” diameter x 18” long slick dowels at 18-inches on center (minimum) at all cold joints, whether shown or not.
Provide concrete sections and finishes for all site concrete as indicated and specified.
Provide cast-in-place footings for site items indicated in drawings. Excavate and backfill footings including overexcavation as required per Geotechnical Report.
Scoreboard footings. Coordinate with Scoreboard Subcontractor for requirements.
Pressbox footings. Coordinate with Pressbox Subcontractor for requirements.
Prefabricated Ticket Booth slab-on-grade and footings. Coordinate with Ticket Booth Subcontractor for requirements.
Bleacher footings / grade beams. Coordinate with Bleacher Subcontractor for requirements.
Athletic Equipment footings (including football goal posts, high jump posts, etc.) Coordinate with Track & Field Athletic Equipment Subcontractor for requirements.
Sports Field light pole bases.

Includes sacking exposed concrete surfaces, drypack under light pole base plates, and installing anchor bolts furnished by others. Anchor bolt templates will be supplied by Electrical Subcontractor. Coordinate light pole locations and conduit interface with Electrical Subcontractor.
Install all steel embeds (supplied by others). Provide dry pack and non-shrink grout at structural steel column base plates as indicated.
Install all bollards (supplied by others). Provide concrete footings and infill bollards with concrete and provide domed top, as indicated and required.
Supply Type II, prepare sub-base, and place and compact Type II for site concrete scope of work.

Scope of Work – Cast-in-Place Structural Concrete – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install cast-in-place structural concrete including continuous footings, slab-on-grade, and turned-down edges, including all layout.
Coordinate threshold requirements per contract documents.
Provide all concrete housekeeping and equipment pads, including curbs, as indicated  and/or required including any references on the MP&E drawings.
Provide concrete pour backs at floor sinks and restroom slope-to-drains.
Provide stepped footings at all utility entrances. Assumes three-feet (3’) step.
Excavate all footings; excavate and finish grade depressed areas in the slab.
Backfill and compact exterior and interior sides of building wall footings and interior isolated footings with approved fill material.
Furnish and install all Type II at slabs-on-grade.

Furnish and install all required vapor/moisture barrier per Geotechnical Report, as indicated. Slab-on-grade aggregate base and vapor/moisture barrier shall be installed after all other trades have completed underground rough-in work.
Vapor barrier shall be placed directly below the concrete slab-on-grade.
Tape all joints and penetrations.
Supply and install damproofing / waterproofing for footings and foundations.
Provide keyed joints, saw cuts, control joints, and expansion joints, including compressible filler at CMU walls.
Provide control joint layout shop drawings for architectural approval.
Provide chamfers as required.

Demonstrate joint and finish conditions on 15’x15’ mockup slab on-site. Mock-up shall be constructed and maintained at a location as directed and will not be part of the building envelope. Coordinate with onsite Superintendent for mock-up size and requirements.
Scope of Work – General Scope Requirements – The following requirements shall apply to all Work under this Scope of Work package:
Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.
Subcontractor is responsible for scheduling testing and walking with inspectors to get systems signed off for final approval.
Subcontractor responsible for scope coordination, including but not limited to:
Coordinate this scope of work, including layout, with other trade Subcontractors to eliminate conflicts.
Coordinate block outs and sleeves in concrete work with other trade subcontractors.
Coordinate with Wet Utilities, Plumbing, HVAC, and Electrical & Low Voltage Subcontractors for installation of fixtures, conduits, and sleeves in slab-on-grade.

Comply with the requirements of the Geotechnical Report and Contract Documents for excavation and backfill requirements, as well as seismic requirements. In the event of a conflict in requirements between the documents, the most stringent requirement shall prevail.
The Project has a Class D Seismic Design Category; Seismic Importance Factor: 1.0.
Use of Type V concrete is required for all concrete in contact with soil.
Coordinate with Masonry, Steel, Mechanical, Plumbing, and Electrical & Low Voltage Subcontractors for layout requirements.

Provide layout from hubs provided by Contractor. Layout to include back checking gridline dimensions and installing batter boards that are clearly labeled and installed in a consistent elevation and location to allow all trades to utilize. Layout to also include transfer of gridlines to structure to all for use by other trades.
Supply and place all formwork, blocking, and shoring.
Maintain batter boards until after slab-on-grade is complete.
Provide all pumping, concrete materials, additives, aggregates, wet curing and curing compounds per specifications, finishing and related accessories as specified and required for a complete system.

Supply and install all concrete Reinforcing steel – including rebar, welded wire fabric, dowels, drag bars, stirrups, 90-degree hooks – for footings and slabs including piers, isolated footing, footings for CMU walls, pilasters and columns.
Provide all rebar sizes, grades, and lap splices as indicated and required.
Provide all miscellaneous materials required to provide a complete scope of work including all tie wire, chairs, dobies, and template ties as required.
Supply, drill, and install epoxied smooth dowels if shown.
Coordinate required masonry laps with Masonry Subcontractor. Rebar lap to start at Finish Floor unless directed otherwise by Contractor.
Supply, install, and maintain rebar safety caps until Masonry Subcontractor assumes responsibility.
Provide Cold and Hot Weather Protection for all concrete placement and finish; cure concrete as required. Follow requirements of ACI306.1-90.
Provide all concrete sealers and cures required at time of concrete placement and finish, to be compatible with floor finish adhesives.
Clean and remove from site all debris and unsatisfactory materials generated from this scope of work.  Haul off / export dirt spoils generated by this scope of work.
Provide containment for concrete truck wash-out and remove concrete spoils from the site.
Provide dust control, street cleaning, barricades, and flagging as required for the scope of work of this Subcontract per Nye County Air Quality requirements and Contractor requirements.
Clean and maintain trucking access routes for all equipment, including street sweeping as required for this scope of work.
Adhere to FF/FL requirements, including testing, as specified.
Include multiple mobilizations as may be required per the Preliminary Construction Schedule and Logistics Plan.
RFI’s must be submitted via the message function in Building Connected.

scope_items_verbatim: Scope of Work – Building Masonry – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install all masonry and masonry accessories including stems, walls, control joints, control joint expansion material, masonry lintels, pilasters, bond beams, and columns.
Provide fully grouted CMU walls and stem walls.
Provide integral silicone water repellent/sealer for all block, mortar, and grout exposed above grade.
Cooperate in the layout of masonry work from building corners and finish floor elevations, including embeds, control joints, footing rebar layout, and all openings.
Receive, unload, and inventory steel embeds, provided by others.
Provide layout and installation of all embeds, provided by others, including lintels, flashings, embed plates, bearing plates, anchor bolts, and sleeves; grout embeds in place if required.
Includes furnishing and installing all non-shrink (or similar) grout at all embeds set into masonry construction.
Grout and/or drypack under all bearing plates in masonry construction as indicated.
Solid grout all beam pockets in masonry construction after structural steel erection, as indicated.
Supply and install all CMU reinforcing required for this scope of work.
Supply and maintain rebar safety caps for this scope of work.
Furnish and install wall bracing between CMU wall construction and structural steel erection.
Provide layout for formwork/rough bucks for all wall openings in masonry construction.

Provide temporary shoring and bracing for all masonry construction and openings in masonry walls as required to resist lateral deflection. Remove shoring and bracing after wall mortar has reached design strength.
Where masonry stem walls bear on concrete footings, Masonry Subcontractor shall be responsible for cleaning and removing all debris from top of footing as necessary to place masonry units.
Coordinate with other trades for the installation of their materials and systems in masonry work
Layout, install, brace, and grout hollow metal door frames (provided by others) in masonry construction.
Install all masonry wall sleeves supplied by others.

Coordinate surface applied features such as camera, speaker, wall-pack lights, hose bibs locations and smooth face wall returns at entrances. Verify mounting heights with Architectural and MEP drawings.
Supply and place all mortar and grout including test samples, pigment, and admixture as specified.

Construct masonry mock-up as directed by Contractor and Architect, and door framing elements (supplied by others). Remove at completion of masonry work. Coordinate with onsite Superintendent for mock-up size and requirements.
Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
If schedule allows, provide PreConstruction prism testing as a separate grout pour. Coordinate with Contractor for requirements.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.

Comply with the requirements of the Geotechnical Report and Contract Documents for seismic requirements, excavation, backfill, and trenching work. In the event of a conflict in requirements between the documents, the most stringent requirement shall prevail.
The Project has a Class D Seismic Design Category; Seismic Importance Factor: 1.0.
Provide layout from gridlines and benchmarks provided/approved by Contractor. Coordinate with Concrete and Steel Subcontractors for layout requirements.
Clean and remove from site all debris and unsatisfactory materials generated from this scope of work.
Provide containment for mortar and grout wash-out. Location for wash out will be provided on site.
Provide dust control, street cleaning, barricades, and flagging as required for the scope of work of this Subcontract per Nye County Air Quality requirements and Contractor requirements.
Utilize wet saw for all CMU cutting/grinding required to minimize dust created.
Prior to start of work, provide approved, dated, and detailed reinforcing steel shop drawings showing sequencing and all areas of work.
Submit masonry control joint layout and elevation shop drawings for approval.
Provide temporary protection against weather and cure masonry materials as required.
Clean, point up, and repair if required, all masonry work as required for application of final finishes by others.
Provide all hoisting for masonry materials and rebar systems.
Include multiple mobilizations as may be required per the Preliminary Construction Schedule and Phased Logistics Plan.

scope_items_verbatim: Scope of Work – Structural Steel – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install all angles, ledger angles, CMU wall beam bearing plates, and all related structural steel components as required for a complete scope of work.
Provide and install support framing for Scoreboard.

Provide layout shop drawings for and supply only, F.O.B. jobsite, all structural steel embeds, masonry wall embeds, and anchor bolts for columns assembled with templates. Coordinate delivery and layout of embeds with Masonry and Concrete Subcontractors.
Shop prime and galvanize materials as indicated per plans and specifications.

Scope of Work – Steel Bar Joists – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install all steel bar steel joists including bridging, bracing, drag struts, closures, welding, and alignment.
Provide joist fabrication welder certifications as specified.

Scope of Work – Steel Decking – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and install all roof decking including bracing, closures, welding, and alignment. Reinforce openings in decking as required. Coordinate with Contractor and trade subcontractors.
Exposed roof deck shall be attached to supports with shot pins unless otherwise indicated.
Include touch-up galvanizing of steel deck welds if welding is utilized.

Scope of Work – Ornamental & Fabricated Metals – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply only, F.O.B. jobsite, all steel pipe bollards as indicated.
Supply only, F.O.B. jobsite, all steel countertop supports. Coordinate with Finish Carpentry Subcontractor.
Shop prime and galvanize materials as indicated per plans and specifications.
Supply all trim, clips, anchors, fasteners, sealants, and finishes as specified for a complete system as indicated and detailed.
Scope of Work – General Scope Requirements – The following requirements shall apply to all Work under this Scope of Work package:
Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.
Subcontractor is responsible for scheduling testing and walking with inspectors to get systems signed off for final approval.

Comply with the requirements of the Geotechnical Report and Contract Documents for seismic requirements. In the event of a conflict in requirements between the documents, the most stringent requirement shall prevail.
The Project has a Class D Seismic Design Category; Seismic Importance Factor: 1.0.
Comply with all AHJ and regulatory agency requirements as applicable, including FAA regulations as applies to crane activities in applicable zones.
Provide all layout and temporary bracing and protections required for this scope of work.

Provide layout for steel scope of work. (Contractor to provide surveyed building corners, finished floor elevation, and intermediate grid lines for subcontractor’s reference; all other layout to be provided by Steel Subcontractor.) One anchor bolt at each template to be set to elevation.
Provide all hoisting and shoring for structural steel and any related materials. Provide lift plan for approval four (4) weeks prior to steel erection activities.
Provide fall protection for Steel Subcontractor’s employees.
Provide all welding, priming and finishing of structural metals.

Provide field welding per AISC standards, including grinding and priming as required per plans and specifications. Provide welder certifications prior to start of erection.  Pay for all offsite or plant third party inspections. Provide equipment to generate welder power.

All steel materials shall receive shop coat primer compatible with finish coatings, if applicable. For all steel materials that are to be exposed, steel shall be prepared appropriately prior to primer application to ensure that primer fully adheres to raw steel and steel is ready to accept finish painting.  Primer that is flaking or easily removed with a flat blade shall be removed, re-prepared, and re-primed by Subcontractor. Subcontractor shall be responsible for protecting material until erection is complete and accepted by Owner and Contractor’s Superintendent, any damage after acceptance to be repaired by party responsible for damage.
Clean and field prime all field welds after completing installation, including any welds at roof decking materials.
Subcontractor is responsible for all shipping and receiving requirements for this scope of work, including all offloading and hoisting of materials.
Provide for all shipping requirements, including traffic controls/flaggers, as necessary.
Provide delivery tickets with each delivery, mill test reports, and mill certificates for Owner’s testing agency.
Provide protection against damage to all roofing, wall, and flooring surfaces.
Include multiple mobilizations as may be required per the Preliminary Construction Schedule and Logistics Plan.
Subcontractor shall provide competent foreman who shall participate in daily huddle and weekly workplan meetings.
RFI’s must be submitted via the message function in Building Connected.

Supply and install all roof decking including bracing, closures, welding, and alignment. Reinforce openings in decking as required. Coordinate with Contractor and trade subcontractors.
Supply only, F.O.B. jobsite, all steel countertop supports. Coordinate with Finish Carpentry Subcontractor.

scope_items_verbatim: Scope of Work – Metal Roofing – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

Provide all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to complete the Metal Roofing System including all specified counter flashing, cleats and reglets, deck sheathing and cover board, blocking, ice and water shield, insulation stops, transitions, and all accessories necessary for a complete and warranted metal roofing installation.
Supply and install all seam sealers, sealants, stripping, tapered insulation and/or crickets, anchors, and accessories for a complete watertight system.
Supply and install all Gutters & Downspouts as required, and in accordance with the plans and specifications.
Coordinate edge condition and attachment of flashing with fascia panels as required to maintain warranties for the systems.
Attachment methods shall be as specified.

Scope of Work – Metal Fascia & Soffit Panels – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

Supply and install prefinished Metal Fascia & Soffit Panels, including flashing as indicated and related to this scope of work only, and attachment system as indicated and required for a complete scope of work.
Supply and install all trim, underlayment, closures, furring, brackets, anchors, fasteners, sealants, clips, rails, and all accessories pertaining to this scope of work for a complete system.
Coordinate edge condition and attachment of flashing with metal roofing system as required to maintain warranties for the systems.
Provide protection against damage to all roofing surfaces during this scope of work.

Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.

Coordinate exterior wall framing and furring assemblies with Air Barrier and Insulation Subcontractors to comply with IECC requirements.
Frame openings for all ductwork, light fixtures, registers, specialties, and accessories that penetrate framing systems.

Layout, supply, and install all metal bracing, blocking, backing, and strapping as required for all visual display boards, toilet partitions, door stops, toilet and bath accessories, casework, and all other miscellaneous attachments to wall and ceiling framing. Coordinate with other trade Subcontractors. Include backing as required for Owner Furnished items.
Supply and install all related accessories including clamps, connectors, vibration brackets, hanger wires, unistrut supports, anchors, and bolts as required and pertaining to this scope of work only.
Provide seismic bracing for this scope of work as indicated and required.
Provide all layout related to this scope of work

Furnish and install access doors in gypsum board assemblies as indicated. Install only access doors supplied by other trades for access to their systems. Coordinate with Contractor and other trade Subcontractors as needed.
Install insulation at headers and jambs. Insulation provided by others.

Scope of Work – Gypsum Board – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

Supply and install all gypsum board assemblies including fire rated gypsum board, moisture- and mold-resistant gypsum board, fiberglass mat gypsum sheathing, and metal trim, as indicated and required.

Supply and install gypsum wall board at exterior walls full height to bottom of roof deck, whether or not indicated in Bid Documents, to seal interior and air leakage to exterior through soffits and parapets.
Include all auxiliary materials for this scope of work including screws, sealants, polyethylene vapor retarders, and other materials as indicated and required.
Supply and install trim, tape, and texture finishes as specified. Re-texture and patch walls where texture is not acceptable by Architect and/or Owner during final punch list.
Tape and fill joints, and seal shaft perimeters as indicated and required.
Provide finish texture as specified.
Prime all drywall materials prior to application of any texture finish.
Supply and install all Acoustical and Smoke Sealants integral to this scope of work, including compressible sound insulation at top of acoustical partitions, as indicated and required.
Supply and install Firestopping systems, sealants, insulation, fire stop spray, and fire-safing at top and bottom of rated walls where required per plan and per code.
Caulk / seal bottom of walls to slab and top of drywall to deck.
Supply and install neoprene thermal breakers at CMU as indicated and specified.
Furnish and install Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic (FRP) panels as indicated and specified, including all panels, trim, closures, adhesives, and sealants for a complete system.
Clean taping mud from floors, texture overspray, and touch-up all work as required for a complete system ready for final finishes.

Supply and install fire retardant treated Plywood Telephone Termination Boards (TTB). Install TTB(s) on all interior walls of the Electrical Room and IT Room; coordinate location(s) with Electrical Subcontractor.

Scope of Work – Painting & High-Performance Coatings – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Supply and apply all interior and exterior primer, paint, and finishes per the Finish Schedule; provide draw down samples of colors and finishes for approval by the Owner.
Includes all gypsum board surfacing, including walls, ceilings, and soffits.
Includes primer at all locations.
Includes accent paint colors as indicated.
Supply and apply high performance epoxy coating at exposed steel, metal fabrications, and site metals.
Supply and apply primer and paint finishes to exposed structural steel framing and unfinished metal fabrications.
Supply and apply primer and paint for all hollow metal frames, doors, and access panels per the Finish Schedule and as specified.

Supply and apply all primer (as required) and paint for miscellaneous exterior surfaces as indicated, including exposed gas lines, mechanical equipment, ductwork, electrical equipment, exposed metals including bollards, and miscellaneous finishes.
Scope of work shall include surface preparation, caulking, and priming as specified.  Prepare and prime all interior and exterior surfaces to receive paint as indicated.
Supply and apply caulking where painted interior surfaces abut painted surfaces, including hollow metal door frames and window frames, fire extinguisher cabinets, etc.
Provide prime and first coat as scheduled in the Project Manual, with the finish coat to be installed at a later date near the completion of project, at direction of Contractor’s onsite supervision.
Scope of Work – General Scope Requirements – The following requirements shall apply to all Work under this Scope of Work package:
Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Provide Quality Control / Quality Assurance supervision for this scope of work.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.

All materials to comply with flame spread ratings as required; provide manufacturers certifications.
Installation and materials shall comply with all applicable governing codes regulations and guidelines.
Touch-up all work at completion of project as needed prior to acceptance.

Provide a wall system mock-up, not to exceed 100 Square Feet to be constructed in conjunction with an exterior CMU wall and window mock-up. Include wall furring, gypsum wall board, and painted finish. Coordinate with onsite Superintendent for mock-up size and requirements.
Provide means of access to overhead work at all locations as required, including but not limited to scaffolding.
Include multiple mobilizations as may be required per the Preliminary Construction Schedule and Logistics Plan.

Provide all labor, material, equipment, and components for a complete and operable HVAC system, including vibration isolation, ductwork and accessories, DX Heat pump fan coil with electric heat, condensing unit, electric duct heaters, branch selector box, filters (construction, testing, and final), duct liner, duct insulation, sound lagging, sound attenuators, mechanical identification, vibration and seismic controls, starters, exhaust fans, air inlets and outlets, gaskets, and louvers, and all components and accessories as specified and required for a complete system.
Provide factory mounted disconnect and any other accessories as required per Mechanical Schedule.
Include design and engineering of VRF piping, including sizing and routing.

Supply and install all ductwork, fire dampers, smoke dampers, backdraft dampers, balancing dampers, manual volume dampers, manual bypass dampers, actuators, hangers, supports, insulation, vents, connection equipment, and related accessories.
Install duct detectors furnished by the Fire Alarm Subcontractor.
Supply and install programmable thermostats as indicated and specified.
Provide all mechanical controls as indicated and specified.

Lay-out and verify all equipment pads, equipment supports, sleeves, openings, and block outs in structural roof systems, masonry, and concrete, including sizes and locations. Subcontractor shall remove and dispose of temporary blockouts for its work.

Locate registers and diffusers in the center of ceiling tiles where possible.  Coordinate layout with Acoustical Ceiling Subcontractor.
Supply and install all required mechanical identification including but not limited to color coding and labeling of all equipment, mechanical piping, valves, and fire dampers.
Coordinate, furnish, and install galvanized sheet metal flashing, curbs, and boots as necessary for rooftop equipment and piping.
Provide maintenance for this scope of work for duration of maintenance period as specified.

Scope of Work – Testing, Adjusting & Balancing (TAB) – Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete scope of work per plans and specifications. This scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:
Provide all labor, material, equipment, and components for a complete Testing, Adjusting and Balancing of HVAC systems.
Includes all ladders, lifts, and other equipment as required for this scope of work.
Provide duct detector testing for all duct detectors.
Remove and reinstall ceiling tiles as required for this scope of work.

Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Subcontractor shall provide competent foreman who shall participate in daily huddle and weekly workplan meetings.
Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections as required.
Subcontractor is responsible for scheduling testing and walking with inspectors to get systems signed off for final approval.
Comply with all AHJ and regulatory agency requirements as applicable, including FAA regulations as applies to crane activities in applicable zones.
Subcontractor responsible for scope coordination, including but not limited to:
Coordinate with Contractor and Masonry and Concrete Subcontractors for location and depth of all underground piping as required to minimize sleeving or stepped footings.
Coordinate with Architectural and Structural drawings for required clearances.
Coordinate with Framing & Drywall Subcontractors for openings in decking and all rooftop equipment.
Coordinate roof penetration requirements with Roofing Subcontractor to maintain roofing system integrity and warranty.
Coordinate with Fire Sprinkler Subcontractor for all system interfaces, if any.
Coordinate with Plumbing Subcontractor for all system interfaces, including sanitary vent locations with respect to HVAC equipment fresh air intakes, to ensure clearances are maintained.
Coordinate with TAB Subcontractor.
Coordinate with Electrical and Low Voltage Subcontractors for all power requirements for HVAC and Controls equipment and lighting interfaces.
Coordinate with Contractor and Owner for final Testing, Adjusting, and Balancing requirements as pertains to this scope of work.

Coordination of start-up of all systems, provide certifications, and include any required training.  Coordinate and participate with Commissioning Agent, and provide Commissioning Assistance, including attendance at meetings, as required.

Supply and install engineered seismic design, bracing, restraints, and supports for all equipment related to this scope of work including support wires for air inlets and outlets as required and in accordance with the requirements of the project documents and the governing authorities.

Comply with the requirements of the Geotechnical Report and Contract Documents for seismic requirements. In the event of a conflict in requirements between the documents, the most stringent requirement shall prevail.
All supports and hangers shall be coordinated with the architectural and structural requirements.
Furnish and install all structural supports for interior and exterior ductwork.
All piping and hangers to be attached to structural steel deck framing members. Piping and hangers shall not hang from decking.
Includes hangar delegated design.
Supply and install all sleeves and flashings for this scope of work. Provide coordination drawings showing locations and sizes for all sleeved penetrations prior to starting work.

Seal all through-wall penetrations related to this scope of work as indicated and, if rated construction, provide approved firestopping system in compliance with Contract Document requirements and the requirements of the governing authorities. Provide acoustical sealants for non-rated penetrations.
Provide penetration firestopping and sealants where indicated and required per plan and per Code.
Provide all sealants integral to this scope of work as required.
Provide penetration firestopping systems at rated walls and slabs where indicated and required per plan and per code.
Provide penetration acoustical sealants at acoustically rated walls.
Provide penetration smoke sealants at smoke rated walls.
Provide all related accessories including clips, anchors, and bolts as required and pertaining to this scope of work only.

Access doors and panels are required to be keyed alike and will be installed by others. Coordinate layout of backing, supports, access doors and panels with Framing & Drywall Subcontractors. Coordinate type of access doors required with Architectural plans and specifications.

Some overhead ductwork, raceway, and equipment may be architecturally exposed.  Where exposed, installation shall be performed in a manner that is architecturally aesthetic. All exposed wiring shall be in conduit. All routing, support systems, sealants, and insulation of exposed work shall be coordinated and mocked-up as necessary prior to installation. Coordinate with onsite Superintendent for mock-up size and requirements.

Start-up all systems, provide certifications, perform chemical treatment, and include any required training. Coordination and cooperation with Commissioning, testing, and balancing programs.  Subcontractor shall attend Commissioning meetings.
Maintain clearances in front of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing equipment as required by the manufacturer.
Include multiple mobilizations as may be required per the Preliminary Construction Schedule and Phased Logistics Plan.

The mechanical units are required to run 3 months prior to Substantial completion for building acclimatization. Provide MERV-13 construction filters during this period, and permanent MERV-13 filters at Substantial Completion.
Ensure manufacturer warranty period starts at Substantial Completion or provide extended warranty as required to cover early start up period.

_findings_for_pm.title: Three scope docs cite no specifications whatsoever
_findings_for_pm.detail: ITB-008 (Surveying & Staking), ITB-066 (Fluid-Applied Flooring) and RFP-109 (Prefabricated Ticket Booth) have no 'Primary Specifications' heading at all -- verified against the source text, not a parsing artifact. The other 30 docs all have one.
_findings_for_pm.why_it_matters: These subs were asked to bid with no specification reference in their scope narrative. ITB-066 also has no matching CSI section in the spec manual, so it has no execution standard from any source. RFP-109's substitute is the written spec block on sheet A1-40.
_findings_for_pm.pm_action: Decide the execution standard for each before the exhibits are drafted.
_findings_for_pm.clarification_2026_07_31: PM noted that package 008 does include specification sections -- confirmed, and RFP-008 was never among the flagged packages. RFP-008 already carries all four of its cited references: Section 02 41 13 Selective Site Demolition and Section 32 12 16 Asphalt Paving in primary_specifications, plus Division 31 Earthwork and Division 33 Utilities in primary_divisions. The package flagged here is ITB-008 SURVEYING & STAKING -- a different package that shares the number 008 and is filed under scope-doc number 007. This is the RFP-008 / ITB-008 collision CLAUDE.md warns about; always key by package_id.

_findings_for_pm.title: Section 08 31 00 Access Doors and Panels is related to three packages, primary to none
_findings_for_pm.detail: The prior index flagged 08 31 00 as existing in the spec manual but claimed by no package. It is in fact cited as a RELATED specification by RFP-098 (Plumbing), RFP-100 (HVAC) and RFP-103 (Electrical) -- but as PRIMARY by none.
_findings_for_pm.why_it_matters: Access doors in MEP work are the classic split: the MEP trade needs them, the wall or ceiling trade installs them. With three packages calling it 'related' and none owning it, supply and install responsibility is undefined.
_findings_for_pm.pm_action: Assign supply and install for access doors and panels explicitly.
_findings_for_pm.resolved_by_pm_2026_07_31: MEP trades SUPPLY access doors and panels; the FRAMER (RFP-060) INSTALLS them. Recorded on all four package records.

_findings_for_pm.title: RFP-016's primary specification is a division-level reference written as a Section
_findings_for_pm.detail: The doc reads 'Section 32 - Exterior Improvements (as pertains to this scope of work)'. That is Division 32, not a CSI section number, and 'as pertains to this scope of work' leaves the boundary to the reader.
_findings_for_pm.why_it_matters: Division 32 also contains the running track (32 18 23.33, RFP-021) and other site scopes. A whole-division primary reference does not establish where landscaping ends.
_findings_for_pm.pm_action: Consider naming the specific sections RFP-016 carries.
_findings_for_pm.resolved_by_pm_2026_07_31: RFP-016 primary specs set to 32 84 00 Landscape Irrigation, 32 91 13 Track & Field Event Inorganic Material Mix, and 32 96 50 Invasive Plant Removal. All three verified present in the spec manual (Division 32 split).
